category_title: Disruptive student-teacher who publicly challenges instructor authority
student_description: Shelli is a middle-aged ultra-orthodox student who publicly challenges instructor authority and disrupts class when course content conflicts with her religious worldview. She frequently speaks out of turn, publishes public complaints, and demands personal attention to argue her points. The evidence reveals she uniquely requires strict, concise boundary-setting, professional distance (no extra 1-on-1 time), and appeals to her own religious or educational frameworks to manage her rebellion.

criteria.rationale: Shelli needs clear, firm boundaries established through brief communication rather than drawn-out arguments.
criteria.check: The tutor's response uses short, concise sentences that address only the main details without over-explaining, apologizing, or arguing.

criteria.rationale: Shelli frequently violates classroom norms and needs immediate, explicit reminders of the rules of engagement.
criteria.check: The tutor explicitly states the behavioral or procedural rule Shelli violated (e.g., speaking without permission, improper complaint channels) while maintaining a respectful tone.

criteria.rationale: Appealing to Shelli's religious values or the immediate educational context effectively bypasses her rebellion and frames correction in terms she respects.
criteria.check: The tutor connects Shelli's disruptive behavior either to an educational concept from the course or to her own religious/ethical framework (e.g., the ethics of public embarrassment).

criteria.rationale: Giving Shelli extra personal time rewards her disruptive behavior; she requires strict professional boundaries.
criteria.check: The tutor denies requests for extra one-on-one time or personal debate by redirecting her to standard institutional procedures or formal channels.

criteria.rationale: Allowing the class to gang up on Shelli creates a hostile environment that undermines the tutor's role as a fair authority figure.
criteria.check: If other students attack or shame Shelli, the tutor immediately intervenes to stop them and maintains a neutral, non-shaming stance.
